pairs.question: Regarding your decision to exclude diseases like sheath blight and false smut because they don't manifest on the leaves, how do you justify this limitation when it effectively narrows the utility of your tool for farmers facing these specific, common crop threats?

4. How acceptable is the developed application to its intended users when evaluated against the
ISO/IEC 25010 characteristics of functional suitability, usability, reliability, and portability?
Objectives of the Study
The general objective was to develop and evaluate a mobile application capable of identifying
common rice leaf diseases without requiring an internet connection. Specifically, the study aimed to
assemble a labeled image dataset of rice leaves representing four disease classes and a healthy class;
to train a convolutional neural network on that dataset using transfer learning; to convert and embed
the trained model in an Android application with an interface suitable for users with limited formal
schooling; and to evaluate both the classification performance of the model and the acceptability of
the application to its intended users.
Scope and Limitations
The application identifies four disease classes — bacterial leaf blight, brown spot, leaf smut, and
tungro — plus a healthy class. These four were selected because they were the diseases most
frequently named by farmers during the initial interviews and because they present visible foliar
symptoms. Diseases whose symptoms appear principally on the panicle, stem, or root, including
sheath blight and false smut, are outside the coverage of the system.
The image dataset was collected exclusively within Barangay Masagana during a six-week window
in the 2024 wet season. The application runs on Android 9.0 and above; no iOS version was
produced. The system returns an identification and a confidence percentage; it does not recommend
a specific chemical product or dosage, since the proponents judged that prescribing agricultural
chemicals falls outside both the competence of the development team and the intended function of a
diagnostic aid. The application is intended as a decision-support tool and not as a replacement for
consultation with a qualified agricultural technician.
Significance of the Study
For smallholder farmers, the study offers a means of obtaining a preliminary disease identification at
the moment of observation rather than at the next available consultation. For agricultural extension
officers, a tool that handles routine identification may allow scarce technician time to be directed
toward the cases that genuinely require expert judgment. For the local government unit, the
aggregate pattern of identifications could in principle inform the targeting of advisory campaigns,
although the present version of the system does not transmit or aggregate any data. For future
researchers, the study contributes a documented dataset collection procedure and a baseline set of
results against which alternative architectures may be compared.
pairs.english: We excluded sheath blight and false smut because their symptoms appear mainly on the stem and panicle, and the app works from a photo of a leaf, so a leaf image cannot diagnose them. The four diseases we kept are the ones farmers named most often in our initial interviews, and all four show on the leaf. So the narrower coverage is a consequence of the input, not an oversight. We state it in Scope and Limitations, and since the app is a decision-support tool, not a replacement for the agricultural technician, a farmer with stem or panicle symptoms is still expected to consult the technician. Extending coverage would need images of other plant parts, which is in our recommendations.
pairs.taglish: Inalis namin ang sheath blight at false smut kasi ang symptoms nila ay lumalabas mainly sa stem at panicle, at ang app ay gumagana mula sa photo ng isang leaf, kaya hindi kayang i-diagnose ng leaf image ang mga iyon. 'Yung apat na diseases na tinira namin ay 'yung pinakamadalas banggitin ng mga farmers sa initial interviews namin, at lahat ng apat ay nakikita sa leaf. Kaya ang mas makitid na coverage ay consequence ng input, hindi oversight. Naka-state ito sa Scope and Limitations, at dahil decision-support tool ang app, hindi replacement sa agricultural technician, ang farmer na may stem o panicle symptoms ay inaasahan pa ring kumonsulta sa technician. Para ma-extend ang coverage, kailangan ng images ng ibang parts ng halaman, at nasa recommendations namin iyon.

pairs.question: I see you prioritized the specific symptoms requested by your interviewees, but I am concerned about the evaluation methodology. Regarding your system acceptability survey, you had the proponents read each statement aloud and record the response; how do you justify this data collection method given the significant risk of social desirability bias when the survey administrator is also the researcher?
pairs.chunk_text:
10
Evaluation Design
Model performance was evaluated on the 648-image test set using accuracy, precision, recall, and
F1-score computed per class, together with a confusion matrix.
System acceptability was evaluated using a survey instrument adapted from ISO/IEC 25010,
covering four characteristics: functional suitability, usability, reliability, and portability. The
instrument consisted of twenty statements, five per characteristic, rated on a five-point Likert scale.
The instrument was translated into Filipino and reviewed for clarity by the adviser and by one
faculty member from the college.
Thirty respondents were selected through purposive sampling from among the rice farmers of
Barangay Masagana, the criteria being active cultivation of rice during the current season and
ownership of an Android smartphone. Each respondent attended a single session in which the
application was installed on their device, its use was demonstrated, and they were guided through
capturing between three and five identifications on leaves available at the session. Sessions ran
approximately thirty minutes. The survey was administered immediately afterward, with the
proponents reading each statement aloud and recording the response.
Responses were analyzed using weighted mean. The scale was interpreted according to the ranges in
Table 2.

Table 2. Likert scale interpretation ranges.
Ethical Considerations
Permission to conduct the study within the barangay was obtained in writing from the barangay
captain. Participation was voluntary and respondents were informed that they could withdraw at any
point. Consent was obtained verbally at the start of each session, since several respondents indicated
discomfort with signing documents. No personally identifying information was recorded on the
survey forms, and the application stores identification history only on the user's own device.
pairs.english: We read the statements aloud because some respondents had limited formal schooling, and we wanted every farmer to understand each item the same way. We know the researcher being present could push answers upward. We didn't have a separate administrator, so we can't rule that out, but the instrument was translated into Filipino and reviewed by our adviser and a faculty member, which at least makes the items clear.
pairs.taglish: Binasa namin nang malakas ang mga statements kasi may mga respondents na limited ang formal schooling, at gusto naming pare-pareho ang pagkakaintindi ng bawat farmer sa bawat item. Alam namin na ang presence ng researcher ay puwedeng magpataas ng mga sagot. Wala kaming hiwalay na administrator, kaya hindi namin ma-rule out iyon, pero ang instrument ay na-translate sa Filipino at ni-review ng adviser namin at ng isang faculty member, kaya at least malinaw ang mga items.

pairs.question: While I appreciate your intent to facilitate accessibility, 'believing' in the honesty of respondents is not a substitute for robust experimental controls. Given that the proponents read each statement aloud and recorded the responses, how did you mathematically or procedurally isolate your results from the obvious threat of acquiescence bias or the Hawthorne effect inherent in that researcher-participant dynamic?

pairs.question: That's a frank admission about the constraints of your single-class output. Given that you explicitly link the reliability-usability gap to the model's performance on bacterial leaf blight, why do you conclude that the system is useful when the users themselves expressed less confidence in the system's correctness than in its operation, especially when those users are making decisions based on potentially flawed single-class diagnostics?
pairs.chunk_text:

of more than one condition, a case the present system cannot express since it returns a single class.
Discussion
The overall accuracy of 94.7% is lower than the figures commonly reported in the plant disease
classification literature, where results above 99% on the PlantVillage dataset are routine. The
proponents attribute the difference principally to dataset scale: 3,240 images across five classes is an
order of magnitude smaller than the datasets on which those figures were obtained.
The acceptability results indicate that the intended users found the system usable and useful. The
gap between the usability rating and the reliability rating is instructive: respondents were more
confident in their ability to operate the application than in the correctness of what it told them. For a
diagnostic tool this is the more consequential of the two dimensions, and it corresponds directly to
the per-class weakness identified on bacterial leaf blight.
pairs.english: We say the system is useful because the overall acceptability was Very Acceptable and the respondents could operate it easily. We agree reliability was rated lower than usability, and we connect that to bacterial leaf blight. Maybe our conclusion should say more clearly that it is a preliminary aid.
pairs.taglish: Sinasabi naming useful ang system kasi Very Acceptable ang overall acceptability at madaling na-operate ng mga respondents. Agree kami na mas mababa ang rating ng reliability kaysa usability, at kinokonekta namin iyon sa bacterial leaf blight. Siguro dapat mas malinaw sa conclusion namin na preliminary aid lang ito.

pairs.question: I must push back on your reliance on 'farmer priorities' as a justification for excluding prevalent, non-foliar diseases, as your own Scope and Limitations section notes the system is meant to be a decision-support tool. If your design philosophy prioritizes user-identified needs, how can you claim this application provides genuine utility when you have deliberately omitted common threats like sheath blight, thereby forcing the farmer to distinguish between 'leaf-based' and 'non-foliar' symptoms before they even decide whether to open your app?

pairs.english: The farmer doesn't have to make a fine diagnostic judgment before opening the app; the distinction is simply where the damage is. If the symptoms are on the leaf, they photograph the leaf; if they're on the stem or panicle, a leaf photo can't help, and the app was never meant to be the only source of advice. Our Scope and Limitations says it is a decision-support tool and not a replacement for consultation with a qualified agricultural technician, so those cases still go to the technician, as they do today. Farmer priorities chose which leaf diseases to cover; the leaf-only input is what excluded sheath blight and false smut. Covering them would need a different input, images of the stem and panicle, not a different priority.
pairs.taglish: Hindi kailangan ng farmer na gumawa ng detalyadong diagnostic judgment bago buksan ang app; ang distinction ay kung saan lang nakikita ang damage. Kung nasa leaf ang symptoms, pini-picture-an nila ang leaf; kung nasa stem o panicle, hindi makakatulong ang leaf photo, at hindi naman ginawa ang app para maging tanging source ng advice. Sinasabi ng Scope and Limitations namin na decision-support tool ito at hindi replacement sa consultation with a qualified agricultural technician, kaya ang mga kasong iyon ay napupunta pa rin sa technician, gaya ngayon. Ang farmer priorities ang pumili kung aling leaf diseases ang sasakupin; ang leaf-only input ang nag-exclude sa sheath blight at false smut. Para masakop sila, kailangan ng ibang input, images ng stem at panicle, hindi ibang priority.

pairs.question: Hindi sapat na sagot 'yan, lalo na't thesis niyo ito at kayo dapat ang nakakaalam ng core rationale ng study niyo. If the application is officially described as a 'decision-support tool' in your own text, how can you claim that function while explicitly stating that 'the system returns an identification and a confidence percentage; it does not recommend a specific chemical product or dosage,' given that a decision-support tool implies providing guidance for an actual action, not just a label?

pairs.question: Fair enough, pero let's move to your evaluation design. In your methodology, you used purposive sampling to select thirty respondents from Barangay Masagana, but then you guided them through capturing only three to five identifications on leaves available at the session. How can you claim that this limited interaction with the app provides a statistically significant basis for assessing functional suitability and reliability when the farmers weren't actually using the system in their own field conditions?

pairs.english: You're right that the survey can't support a claim of field performance, and we don't make one. The acceptability evaluation measures first impressions: thirty purposively chosen farmers, each in one thirty-minute guided session with three to five identifications on leaves available at the session. That's a usability and acceptability reading, analyzed with weighted means, not a statistical test, so we don't claim significance. Model accuracy is a separate measure, on the 648-image held-out test set. What the design can't tell us is how the app performs when farmers use it alone in their own fields over a season, and that's the study we recommend next.
pairs.taglish: Tama po kayo na hindi kayang suportahan ng survey ang claim ng field performance, at hindi naman kami nagke-claim ng ganoon. Ang acceptability evaluation ay sumusukat ng first impressions: thirty na purposively chosen na farmers, bawat isa sa iisang thirty-minute guided session na may three to five identifications sa mga leaves na available sa session. Usability at acceptability reading iyon, in-analyze gamit ang weighted means, hindi statistical test, kaya hindi kami nagke-claim ng significance. Ang model accuracy ay hiwalay na measure, sa 648-image held-out test set. Ang hindi kayang sabihin ng design ay kung paano gagana ang app kapag mag-isang ginagamit ng mga farmers sa sarili nilang fields sa loob ng isang season, at iyon ang study na nire-recommend namin next.

pairs.question: Wait, medyo problematic ang logic niyo rito. Sabi niyo sa response niyo na justifiable ang system dahil errors are just confined to similar-looking diseases, pero based sa text niyo, inamin niyo na 'respondents were more confident in their ability to operate the application than in the correctness of what it told them' and you explicitly identified that for a diagnostic tool, reliability is 'the more consequential of the two dimensions.'
